content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in San Francisco

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Review PMI's baseline requirements—typically a high school diploma plus substantial hours leading projects—before you apply. Granite PM Academy's eligibility advisors can clarify whether your background qualifies.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. The instructor-led course covers all five process groups and ten knowledge areas tested on exam day. Flexible scheduling lets you complete hours around your current role at firms like Salesforce, Visa, or Wells Fargo.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the bootcamp, submit your official PMP application directly to PMI, documenting your education and project experience. Pay PMI's exam fee at the time of application. Granite PM Academy provides guidance on the application portal and required documentation.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and Q&A sessions—to build confidence before test day. You'll take the four-hour, 180-question PMP exam at a Pearson VUE testing center in the Bay Area. Our instructors remain available to clarify concepts during your final review.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, you earn the PMP credential valid for three years. Maintain it by earning professional development units (PDUs) through continuing education, volunteering, or giving talks. PMI's online platform tracks your progress toward renewal, keeping your credential current as your career advances.
